messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Complex bifactor model: R won't run (crashes). help!
parts:
Andy,
  First a caveat, then some thoughts.  The caveat:  I find it much easier to think through and debug complex models by started at zero and explicitly coding each aspect of the model using lavaan() with no convenience parameters than to start with part of the model specified by default and work backwards by removing parameters.  Perhaps that is just a matter of personal style.

  If I understand correctly, your model has 18 factors, 17 specific plus a general factor.  Your model specifies these as all being orthogonal to one another.

  The standard bifactor model allows the specific factors to covary and only requires that the general factor be orthogonal to the specific factors.

  Typically, items from different scales have non-zero correlations.  Oblique models account for such correlations without giving up simple structure by allowing the factors to correlate.  One can trace a path from and item on one scale, up to its factor, across a covariance to another factor, and down to an item on another scale.

  Orthogonal models do not allow the factors to covary and must therefore account for cross-scale correlations in another way.  Typically, this is done by giving up simple structure and allowing items to cross-load on factors for other scales.

  Your model is essentially an orthogonal model with a general factor added.  This general factor must alone account for all the correlations between items across scales.  With such a large number of diverse items, it may be unrealistic to expect a single dimension of covariation to entirely account for all the cross-scale correlations.

  I would first suggest that you reconsider whether you really meant the specific factors to be orthogonal.  If so, then I would start small, perhaps with two scales, and gradually build up the model until it starts to show problems.  Each time you add to the model, monitor what happens with the residuals.  This strategy may help you isolate the source of the problems.

  If none of that helps, I would suggest being more descriptive about exactly what happens when you try fit the model.  The term "crash" is vague and could refer to convergence to an improper solution, convergence failure, the lavaan function terminating early within R, or the R program itself closing on your computer.  Also, if you can reproduce the same behavior in a simple self-contained example that others can run, that may help facilitate an answer.

Keith

Keith A. Markus

http://jjcweb.jjay.cuny.edu/kmarkus

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: Complex bifactor model: R won't run (crashes). help!
parts: R runs the model but the output cannot be viewed fully (I scroll up and only half the output is displayed).

If you are using RStudio, go to: Tools, Global Options, Code, Display, and under Console it says:
"Limit length of lines displayed". Make that number bigger.

You can also run the sink() function, or run R in command line mode and have output sent to a text file (essentially what Mplus does), or use various extractor functions to look at the part of the output you are interested in.

Jeremy
